glossary: Level
The latest reading itself, compared with every reading in the series' own history.
Level: at or above

The share of the readings in the series' history that the latest is at or above, counted from the lowest. 100% is the highest reading in that history; near 0% is near the lowest. It says where the reading sits, not whether that is good or bad.
Change over 12 months

The latest reading minus the reading 12 months earlier. For a rate, a spread or an index around zero it is in points; for a level that grows (prices, jobs, output, credit, claims, debt) it is a percent of the earlier reading. Weekly and daily series count whole weeks (12 months is 52), as FRED does; a day with no reading that many weeks before has no change.
Typical move

1.4826 times the median distance of a series' changes from their median change: for changes shaped like a bell, about one standard deviation, but a spike does not widen it. It is the measure the loss thresholds use for ordinary year-to-year movement.
Normal range
The median change in the series' history plus or minus one typical move. Each series has its own.
Increasing, Stable, Decreasing

Stable: the change is inside its normal range. Increasing: at or above its top. Decreasing: at or below its bottom. For a series that usually grows, such as prices, Increasing means growing faster than it normally does and Decreasing slower, or falling. None of the three says better or worse.
Typical moves (a number)

How far the change is from the median change, in typical moves: +2.0 is two typical moves above it. The same scale for every series, so their moves can be compared; the Dashboard draws two together on it.
Since
The first of the unbroken run of changes, up to the latest, that read the same way, each read against the same normal range.
History from
The first reading each series is measured against. Every series is measured against its full history.
Quarters left out
Quarters the firm takes out of every history: none at present. A reading in one is not measured against and not drawn; a change with either end in one is not counted.
Off the chart

A chart's axis may leave off up to 1% of its readings at each end, so a spike does not flatten the rest; a note under the chart names the furthest. The latest reading and the normal range always stay on, and no reading changes.
Change only
A level that climbs over the decades with prices and the economy sits near the top of its own history in almost every year, so its place there says nothing. Only its change is read.
In the research
Which way the research says a series signals stress, where it says so. It is shown on each series' tab as a fact about the research and changes no reading.
Sahm reading

The 3-month average unemployment rate minus its lowest 3-month average in the 12 months before. Sahm's published trigger is 0.50. Shown beside the change, never used to read it. Where a month has no value (October 2025), the average is taken from the two months that do, as FRED does.
Pulled
The day the data was downloaded. Every pull is kept in its own folder, so a reading can always be traced to the release it used.
No value published
A period the publisher left blank, such as October 2025 (the lapse in appropriations). It stays empty: never filled, never read as zero.
Made from two series
House prices against income, and the mortgage rate over the 10-year Treasury, are worked out from two series in the same pull. Each tab says how.
Break
A change in how the publisher builds the series, or a known seasonal step, that a reader should know before comparing across it.
Not read
A reading the catalog holds that the pull could not supply or that has too little history. The Not read tab says which and why, when there are any.
Usable with care
A series from the research's usable-with-care group: short, broken or heavily revised. It is read the same way as the rest, with why it needs care beside it.
Household debt
The NY Fed's household debt by type, as its Quarterly Report on Household Debt and Credit gives it, from the New York Fed Consumer Credit Panel / Equifax.
Dashboard
Pick any two series to see together: both changes in typical moves, both levels as where they sit in their own histories, and each one's own charts.
As you have it
The readings from the firm's settings file, settings.json: every reading on every other tab.
What if
The same pull read with a second settings file, what-if-pandemic-left-out.json. It changes no reading anywhere else in the workbook, and neither file is changed.
Move
From Decreasing through Stable to Increasing: ▲ when the what-if reads a change more upward, ▼ more downward.
Dashed lines
On a series' change chart: its normal range under the what-if, over the years its history covers. Drawn only where the two count the change over the same months.
